trial_name: CATS — Norepinephrine plus Dobutamine vs Epinephrine Alone in Septic Shock (2007)
citation: Annane D, Vignon P, Renault A, Bollaert P-E, Charpentier C, Martin C, et al; CATS Study Group. Norepinephrine plus dobutamine versus epinephrine alone for management of septic shock: a randomised trial. Lancet. 2007;370(9588):676-684.
trial_type: RCT — prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group trial
one_liner: Epinephrine alone produced similar 28-day and 90-day mortality compared to a strategy of norepinephrine plus selective dobutamine in adults with early septic shock.

pico.population: Adult ICU patients within 24 hours of early septic shock requiring catecholamines after initial fluid resuscitation.
pico.intervention: Epinephrine alone (started at 0.2 mcg/kg/min) titrated to MAP >= 70 mmHg plus placebo inotrope infusion.
pico.comparison: Norepinephrine (started at 0.2 mcg/kg/min) titrated to MAP >= 70 mmHg plus dobutamine (5 mcg/kg/min titrated as needed for low cardiac index/hypoperfusion).

background.existing_knowledge: Septic shock management routinely requires vasoactive therapy after fluid resuscitation. Norepinephrine was widely used first-line with dobutamine added for suspected low cardiac output, while epinephrine offered single-agent vasopressor and inotropic properties.
background.knowledge_gap: Uncertainty existed regarding whether a single-agent epinephrine strategy or a combined norepinephrine plus dobutamine strategy was superior or safer in early septic shock.
background.hypothesis: Norepinephrine plus dobutamine would improve outcomes or offer a superior safety profile compared with epinephrine alone by avoiding epinephrine-associated metabolic and chronotropic adverse effects.

methods.design: Prospective, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group trial (19 ICUs in France); central randomization stratified by center with block size 6.

inclusion: Age >= 18 years in adult ICU within < 24 hours of meeting shock criteria
Suspected or identified infection plus SIRS
Hypotension (MAP < 70 mmHg or SBP < 90 mmHg) requiring catecholamines after fluid bolus >= 1000 mL or PCWP 12–18 mmHg
Requirement of dopamine > 15 mcg/kg/min or any dose of epinephrine or norepinephrine
At least 2 organ dysfunctions/hypoperfusion signs: PaO2/FiO2 < 280, urine output < 0.5 mL/kg/h or < 30 mL/h for >= 1 h, arterial lactate > 2 mmol/L, platelets < 100x10^9/L

methods.intervention: Epinephrine started at 0.2 mcg/kg/min, titrated by 0.2 mcg/kg/min increments to MAP >= 70 mmHg, plus placebo inotrope infusion.
methods.comparison: Norepinephrine started at 0.2 mcg/kg/min (titrated by 0.2 mcg/kg/min to MAP >= 70 mmHg) plus dobutamine 5 mcg/kg/min (titrated by 5 mcg/kg/min increments as needed per protocol).
methods.blinding: Double-blind using identical pharmacy-prepared syringes and placebo dobutamine infusion.
methods.sample_size_power: Planned n=340 to detect a 20% absolute mortality reduction (from 60% to 40%) with 95% power at 5% two-sided alpha. Enrolled n=330.
secondary_outcomes: Time to hemodynamic success (MAP >= 70 mmHg for >= 12 consecutive hours)
Time to vasopressor withdrawal (first study drug interruption for >= 24 hours)
Total fluid infused until catecholamine withdrawal
methods.follow_up: 28 days for primary endpoint; 90 days for long-term mortality.

headline_bullets: No statistically significant difference in 28-day all-cause mortality between epinephrine alone and norepinephrine plus dobutamine (40% vs 34%, P=0.31).
Pressor-free days to day 28 were slightly higher with norepinephrine plus dobutamine (median 22 vs 20 days, P=0.05).
Epinephrine caused early transient metabolic and chronotropic effects, including higher lactate, lower arterial pH (days 1–4), and higher heart rate.

outcomes_table.outcome: Time to hemodynamic success (MAP >= 70 mmHg for >= 12h)
Total fluid infused until catecholamine withdrawal

safety: Ventricular arrhythmias occurred in 12/161 (7%) patients in the epinephrine arm and 8/169 (5%) in the norepinephrine + dobutamine arm.
Epinephrine caused early metabolic alterations, including higher serum lactate levels, lower arterial pH on days 1–4, and higher heart rates on days 1–4.
A published erratum clarified statement details regarding arterial pH and corrected a figure panel.

domains.notes: Central randomization stratified by center in blocks of 6; adequate allocation concealment via blinded pharmacy preparation.
Double-blinded using identical syringes and placebo dobutamine infusion with protocolized titration algorithms.
Very low attrition; intention-to-treat analysis; 1 patient withdrew consent on day 3.
High initial delivery (156/161 epinephrine; 166/169 NE+dobutamine); switching was allowed for refractory failure.
Well-balanced SAPS II and SOFA scores, though epinephrine group was slightly older (median 66 vs 63 years).

internal_validity.verdict: Internal validity is moderate-to-strong due to double-blinding and minimal attrition, though limited by underpowering for small effects.

domains.notes: Adult septic shock in French ICUs; excluded acute MI, PE, severe neutropenia, and care limitations.
Applicable to settings with protocolized hemodynamic monitoring; conducted prior to modern Sepsis-3 definitions.

external_validity.verdict: External validity is moderate, restricted to adult ICUs with intensive protocolized monitoring.

strengths: Double-blind, multicenter randomized design in severe ICU shock.
Pragmatic strategy-level comparison using realistic clinical algorithms.
Clear operational definitions for hemodynamic outcomes and high follow-up completion.
limitations: Targeted an unrealistically large 20% absolute mortality reduction, leaving the trial underpowered for realistic smaller differences.
Permitted crossover/switching between strategies for refractory shock.
Exact daily metabolic values were not fully tabulated in the main text.

critical_appraisal.summary: A well-executed double-blind trial demonstrating clinical equivalence between vasopressor strategies, limited mainly by sample size power.
weaknesses: Sample size of 330 was underpowered for modest mortality differences
Pragmatic strategy crossover blurred pure pharmacological comparison

sections.authors_conclusion: Epinephrine alone and norepinephrine plus dobutamine produce similar survival rates at 28 and 90 days in adults with early septic shock.

clinical_bottom_line.verdict: Epinephrine alone is an acceptable alternative to norepinephrine plus dobutamine, though norepinephrine remains the preferred first-line agent in guidelines.
clinical_bottom_line.applies_to: Adult ICU patients with early septic shock requiring vasoactive support.
clinical_bottom_line.does_not_mean: Does not mean transient epinephrine-induced lactic acidosis indicates worsening tissue ischemia.
implementation_caveats: Expect higher early lactate and lower arterial pH during initial epinephrine administration.
Do not use serial lactate trends as the sole target for resuscitation when epinephrine is infusing.

controversies.notes: Targeting a 20% absolute mortality reduction (60% to 40%) made the study underpowered to exclude smaller, clinically meaningful mortality differences.
Epinephrine's beta-2 agonist mediated lactate generation confounds lactate-guided resuscitation strategies.

context_related_trials.relation: Compared dopamine to norepinephrine in shock, demonstrating fewer arrhythmias and lower mortality in septic shock with norepinephrine.
Evaluated early low-dose norepinephrine in septic shock, reinforcing norepinephrine as the primary baseline vasopressor.

unresolved_questions: Whether epinephrine impacts mortality in specific phenotypic subgroups with acute septic cardiomyopathy.
The true precision of epinephrine vs NE+dobutamine in modern Sepsis-3 bundle care paradigms.

quick_recall.one_line_takeaway: Epinephrine alone achieves similar overall survival to norepinephrine plus dobutamine in septic shock, but induces early metabolic lactate elevations.
